Where it began

Prithvi Shaw was born on 9 November 1999 and grew up in Virar, in Maharashtra. He learned his cricket in Mumbai, with the Middle Income Group club and at Rizvi Springfield High School, whom he captained to the Harris Shield, the city's great schools competition, in 2012 and 2013. In 2013 he appeared in a documentary film, Beyond All Boundaries.

England played its part too. In 2012 he spent two months playing for Cheadle Hulme School in Manchester, where he made 1,446 runs and took 68 wickets, and he returned for more English club cricket the following summer.

The player

A right-handed opening batter, he made a hundred on his first-class debut for Mumbai, in a Ranji Trophy semi-final, and another on his Duleep Trophy debut, matching a pair of feats Sachin Tendulkar had managed before him. In 2018 he captained India to the Under-19 World Cup.

Later that year he made his Test debut against West Indies and scored 134 in his first innings. At 18 he was younger than any Indian before him to make a hundred on Test debut, and he was player of the series. His Test career was a brief one: five Tests between 2018 and 2020, bringing 339 runs at 42.38 with a hundred and two fifties.

What made him special

He liked to score quickly from the start. In 2021 he hit six fours in the opening over of an IPL innings, only the second man to do that in the competition. In the Vijay Hazare Trophy that year he made 227 not out against Pondicherry and 827 runs in the season, and in January 2023 he made 379 against Assam in the Ranji Trophy.

The Test arena proved harder to hold on to than to reach, and Australia in December 2020 was a tough place to bat. Not many players manage a fifty in New Zealand and a hundred at home inside five Tests, though, and he did both.

Away from the middle

He was, at the time, the youngest man to open the batting in the IPL when he walked out for Delhi in April 2018, and a few days later he became the joint youngest to make a fifty in the competition. He has also led sides: Mumbai to the Vijay Hazare Trophy in 2021, and North Mumbai Panthers to the Mumbai League title in 2019.

In 2025 he moved to Maharashtra and began with a hundred in his first innings for them, then made 222 off 156 balls against Chandigarh in the Ranji Trophy.

And finally

In November 2013, four days after Tendulkar retired from international cricket, the schoolboy Shaw made 546 in a Harris Shield match, with 85 fours. Tendulkar had once made 326 in the same competition. Somewhere a Mumbai scorer had to sharpen a lot of pencils.
